newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-PLO summit, deal could be today - Israel.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-PLO summit, deal could be today - Israel.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat are likely to meet on Thursday to close a deal giving Palestinians self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron, an Israeli official said.

"It's almost definite that there will be some kind of a summit this afternoon...and probably will be a final meeting in which the agreement will be initialled," Netanyahu's adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters.

"There are no outstanding issues unless the Palestinians raise a new issue or demand the reopening of an issue that has been concluded," Bar-Illan said. He said the chances of a meeting on Thursday were about 90 percent.
Palestinian negotiator Jamil al-Tarifi said no summit had been set. He said differences remained over target dates for future Israeli redeployments in West Bank rural areas.
"Until now there are no arrangements for a meeting," Tarifi told Reuters.

If initialled on Thursday, the deal could go to Israel's cabinet on Friday for approval and be signed and given Israeli parliamentary approval in time for a redeployment early next week, Bar-Illan said.

Under a 1995 Israeli-PLO peace deal, 80 percent of Hebron was due to be given self-rule nine months ago. But violence, security concerns and other issues have held up the handover. Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
